title: Unchecked property access on socket.handshake in getSocketIp
test: Scratch check socket-check-20-handshake.js.txt (lane `socket` scratchpad), run on dev bfe4d26 and on an archive of ac1c688: (1) a real socket.io 4.8.4 server with registerSocketHandlers(io, {}, {}), so the default resolver getSocketIp is used, records socket.handshake in io.use() middleware and in 'connection', then a websocket client and a polling client each emit join-room {code:'ABCDEF'}; (2) a hand-made socket with no handshake fed to registerSocketHandlers through a fake io, with the default resolver and with a resolver that never reads handshake. Also existing tests on the default resolver: node --test tests/socketTransportRecovery.test.js tests/socketRelayBootstrap.test.js (10 pass)
proof: The claim does not hold as a defect. It is right that lib/socket.js:275 `return normalizeIp(socket.handshake.address || 'unknown')` has no optional chaining and would throw if handshake were missing, but nothing in Nextra can pass such a socket. (a) socket.io always builds handshake in the Socket constructor, before middleware and 'connection' run: node_modules/socket.io/dist/socket.js:121 `this.handshake = this.buildHandshake(auth)`, with address = this.conn.remoteAddress. The check saw hasHandshake true and address '127.0.0.1' at both stages for both transports, and join-room answered 'Room not found.' (the IP lookup ran without throwing). (b) The running server does not call getSocketIp: server.js:1597 passes `getClientIp: getSocketHandshakeIp` to registerSocketHandlers, and lib/socket.js:1797-1799 uses getSocketIp only when no getClientIp is given (some tests). (c) Even a hand-made socket without handshake does not crash anything: both call sites (create-room, lib/socket.js:1843; join-room, :2021) are inside try/catch, so the join-room reply was {success:false, error:'Internal error'} and the log 'join-room error: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'address')'; the same socket with a resolver that never reads handshake got 'Room not found.', so the throw does come from line 275. Original code: getSocketIp is byte-identical at ac1c688 (lines 263-276, the lines the claim cites), server.js there passes getSocketHandshakeIp too (line 1568, since 30ef97f), and the same check on an archive of ac1c688 gave the same output. So the defect was not real on the original code either. No file changed.
